items.title: Quoting Addy Osmani, Morgan Westlee Lunt, and Qing Wang
items.summary:
We think "did a human read the code?" is an imprecise proxy for "what could go wrong with this change, and which check—automated or human—is the right one to catch it?"
Asking that question also changed when review happens. Before, review was a gate at the end of the road: write the code, open a PR, wait for your colleague.
Now, review runs continuously, more like spellcheck while you write. Most changes have been reviewed and fixed by Claude at least once before a human is asked to look. This catches most routine mistakes, and saves team attention for higher-level questions and scrutiny.

items.title: David's Bridal built a wedding-planning agent with tens, not hundreds
items.summary: Enterprise: After 76 years of only selling dresses and a 2023 bankruptcy, the country's largest wedding dress retailer is pivoting 180 degrees into AI-powered wedding planning — a marketplace play with an agentic twist, anchored on first-party bride data. President Elena Vilk says what would have taken 100-plus people was built with tens using standard agentic coding tools: 'There's no way we could have achieved anything like this even three years ago.'

items.title: 'Software is over': a developer one-shots Photoshop
items.summary: Business: Brandon Thomas used Claude Opus to decompile Photoshop and reconstruct it as a clean-room rebuild — a copyright workaround that used to require two teams of engineers and is now practical for an individual. He's since bootlegged the entire Adobe suite and offers a buggy but free version of software Adobe prices at $100 a month; Adobe stock opened 3% lower when the story went viral.

items.title: The labs are now racing on speed
items.summary: Compute: Anthropic is serving Opus 5.5 at a verified 285 tokens per second on its upgraded Fast Mode, while OpenAI's docs suggest a 280 theoretical max for GPT-6-1 Sol — at a 50% price premium. items.title: A 2026 model trapped in a 2025 harness
items.summary: Models: Google didn't just miss eight months of coding-model development — it missed eight months of harness UX iteration. Anti-Gravity lacks cloud environments, SSH, a built-in browser, and smart permission checks, leaving users clicking constant pop-ups or running unrestricted turbo mode. When a model is good enough to force you through a bad harness, that tells you something.
